hints: Focus on reducing power down Group 17, chloride is weak but iodide is a very strong reducing agent.
Notice that chloride only does an acid-base reaction to give colourless HCl, so it is not oxidised and no colour appears.
Consider what iodide does to concentrated sulfuric acid and what coloured products like iodine would tell you, then count which statements fit.
walkthrough:
**Recall the key trend**

Think like this, concentrated sulfuric acid is both an acid and an oxidising agent. Whether it oxidises a halide depends on how good a reducing agent the halide ion is.

Reducing strength: $\text{Cl}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{I}^-$

**Check sodium chloride**

Chloride is too weak to reduce sulfur from +6. It only acts as a base and takes a proton.

$$\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{NaHSO}_4 + \text{HCl}$$

$\text{HCl}$ is a colourless gas with white fumes, so there is no colour change. This makes both statement 1 and statement 2 correct.

**Check sodium iodide**

Iodide is a powerful reducing agent. It reduces $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{S}$ and even $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, while it is itself oxidised to purple-black iodine.

$$8\text{HI} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 4\text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{S} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

So statement 3 is also correct. With 1, 2 and 3 all correct, the combination for all three is the answer.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Chloride is not oxidised and gives only colourless HCl, while iodide is oxidised to coloured iodine products.
options.B: Incorrect, this combination leaves out statement 3. Students choose this if they forget how strongly reducing iodide is and think it behaves like chloride.
options.C: Incorrect, this combination leaves out statement 1. Students choose this if they confuse acid-base reaction of chloride with oxidation, even though oxidation number of Cl stays at -1 in HCl.
options.D: Incorrect, this is statement 1 only. Students choose this if they doubt the observation statements and do not link purple iodine vapours and yellow sulfur to oxidation of iodide.
